prompt_text: AI to draft donor thank you letters
response_text:
You can absolutely use AI to draft donor thank you letters; the best approach is to have AI create a strong first draft and then quickly personalize it yourself before sending.[5][7]

Here’s a practical way to do it, plus a ready-made prompt you can paste into any AI tool (including this one).

---

### 1. How to use AI effectively for donor thank you letters

Fundraising experts recommend using AI for the *thankfulness* (the words, formatting, and speed) while you provide the *gratitude* (the personal, human touches).[5][7]

A simple workflow is:

1. **Collect key details**  
   - Donor name  
   - Gift amount or description  
   - Purpose of the gift / fund / program  
   - One concrete impact detail or story  
   - Your organization’s name, mission, and signatory  
   AI tools and CRMs can even pull much of this automatically.[5]

2. **Use a well-structured AI prompt**  
   Gail Perry Group and other fundraising trainers provide prompts specifically for donor thank you letters that stress warm, upbeat, jargon‑free language, impact focus, and first/second person (“I,” “we,” “you”).[1][2]

3. **Generate the draft in your AI tool of choice**  
   - You can paste a prompt into tools like ChatGPT, Gemini, or specialized fundraising tools such as Fundwriter or FreeWill’s “Thank you notes” assistant, which are built to generate donor letters from your mission and gift details.[1][3][6][8]

4. **Human review and personalization**  
   - Experts emphasize always reviewing the AI draft and adding a personal note or specific reference (e.g., “I loved meeting you at the breakfast briefing last week”) before sending.[1][5][7]

---

### 2. A ready-made AI prompt you can use

Paste this into your AI tool and fill in the brackets (you can also use it directly with me):

> You are an experienced nonprofit fundraising professional. Draft a short, warm donor thank you letter.
>  
> Details:  
> - Donor name: [DONOR NAME]  
> - Gift amount/type: [AMOUNT OR DESCRIPTION]  
> - Date or occasion of gift: [DATE / OCCASION]  
> - Organization name: [ORG NAME]  
> - Mission (1–2 sentences): [MISSION]  
> - How the gift will be used (program/fund): [USE / PROGRAM]  
> - Specific impact or outcome (be concrete): [IMPACT DETAIL OR EXAMPLE]  
> - Relationship/history with donor (if any): [NEW DONOR / RETURNING / LONGTIME SUPPORTER / EVENT ATTENDEE, ETC.]  
> - Signer’s name and title: [NAME, TITLE]  
> - Signer contact info (optional): [PHONE / EMAIL]  
>  
> Writing requirements:  
> - Write in the first person (“I,” “we”) and speak directly to the donor (“you”) multiple times.[1]  
> - Open with a creative, engaging first sentence that immediately conveys gratitude and makes the donor feel special.[1]  
> - Be warm, positive, and upbeat; avoid formal or stiff language.  
> - Clearly connect the donor’s gift to the organization’s mission and the impact it will have (“Because of your gift…”).[1][2]  
> - Keep it concise (about 1/2 page to 1 page), with short paragraphs.  
> - Use contractions (we’ll, you’re) and a natural, conversational tone.[1]  
> - Do *not* use generic jargon like “on behalf of,” “we are deeply grateful for your continued support,” or “Dear Friend.”[1]  
> - Do not ask for anything else in this letter (no additional appeals).[1]  
> - End with a warm closing and an optional P.S. that reinforces impact or appreciation.  
>  
> Output the letter ready to send, starting with an appropriate salutation.

---

### 3. Example of an AI-generated donor thank you letter

Here is a generic example (I can customize this if you give me real details):

> Dear Alex,  
>  
> Your generosity just opened a new door for a student who’s been waiting for a chance like this.  
>  
> Thank you for your recent gift of $500 to **Bright Futures Learning Center**. Because of you, we’ll be able to provide after‑school tutoring and a hot meal to children who are falling behind in reading and math.  
>  
> Our mission is simple: to ensure every child in our community has the support they need to succeed in school and in life. Your gift is already helping us hire additional tutors and extend our program hours so more students can get one‑on‑one attention.  
>  
> I can’t begin to thank you enough for believing in our kids. When you give, you’re not just funding a program—you’re giving a child the chance to feel confident walking into class each morning.  
>  
> We’re absolutely thrilled to have your support, and I hope you’ll feel proud every time you think about the students whose lives you’re touching.  
>  
> With gratitude,  
>  
> Jordan Rivera  
> Executive Director, Bright Futures Learning Center  
> 555‑123‑4567  
>  
> P.S. Because of your gift, three additional students will receive daily tutoring for the rest of the semester—thank you for making that possible.

---

### 4. Tools designed specifically for donor thank yous

If you prefer specialized tools instead of general chatbots:

- **Fundwriter.ai** – Built for nonprofits; generates personalized donor thank you letters and other fundraising copy from simple inputs like mission, project description, and gift details.[6]  
- **FreeWill “Thank you notes” tool** – A simple web form where you enter who you’re thanking, gift type, and your nonprofit name; it generates a customized note.[8]  
- **Template-based prompts** from fundraising educators (e.g., Gail Perry Group, AI for Education) give you tested language frameworks you can reuse in any AI chatbot.[1][2]

---

If you share:
- your organization’s name and mission,  
- the type of gift (amount, purpose), and  
- who the donor is (new/returning/major/event, etc.),  

I can draft one or more customized thank you letters you can use immediately.
